item.title: Middle East live: First Gaza flotilla activists deported by Israel arrive in Turkey
item.description: The first group of foreign activists from the Global Sumud aid flotilla arrived in Turkey on Thursday after Israel deported them following global outcry over their treatment in custody. A viral video released Wednesday showed Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir heckling the detained activists as they were bound and kneeling. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Israel's Ben-Gvir sees 'no innocent people in Gaza or even Europe': Journalist Gideon Levy
item.description: FRANCE 24's François Picard welcomes veteran Israeli journalist and Haaretz columnist Gideon Levy. He offers a scathing analysis of Israeli politics, the Gaza war, the unprecedented rise of xenophobic nationalism and Israel's growing dependence on the United States. Speaking from Tel Aviv amid mounting electoral tensions, Levy argues that "everything – war and peace, domestic politics, legislation – is now covered by the shadow of the upcoming elections".

item.title: Trump says US may hit Iran again, claims Tehran wants deal
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that the United States may need to attack Iran again and claimed that he had been only an hour away from deciding ‌on a fresh strike before he allegedly postponed the attack. Thousands of people have been killed in Iran, Lebanon and the wider Middle East since the US-Israeli war against Iran began at the end of February. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Iran examines new US proposal as Trump says talks are in 'final stages'
item.description: Iran on Wednesday said it was examining a new US proposal, transmitted by mediator Pakistan, to end the war in the Middle East even as the two sides continued to trade threats over resuming attacks. Speaking in Washington, US President Donald Trump told reporters that negotiations were in their “final stages”. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Iran ‘prefers diplomacy’ but if there’s a war, Tehran says it’s ready
item.description: Iran and the US traded threats as President Donald Trump warned of renewed strikes a day after he said he held off a major assault in hopes of a peace deal. Reporting from Tehran, FRANCE 24’s Reza Sayah says Iranian officials have maintained their position that “they prefer diplomacy. They don't see a military solution to this conflict,” he explains. “But if there's a war, they're ready for it.”

item.title: Israel far-right finance minister says ICC prosecutor seeks arrest warrant against him
item.description: Israel's far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said on Tuesday the International Criminal Court prosecutor had sought an arrest warrant against him, blaming the Palestinian Authority for the move. Smotrich said Israel would respond by ordering the evacuation of the Palestinian Bedouin community of Khan al-Ahmar in the occupied West Bank.

item.title: US, Iran trade threats as Tehran stages mass weddings for couples ready for 'sacrifice'
item.description: President Donald Trump warned Tuesday that the United States may strike Iran again, but Tehran's army threatened to open "new fronts" if he went ahead. In the capital, Iranian authorities held mass public weddings for couples who signed up to a state-sponsored scheme declaring their readiness to sacrifice their lives in the war against the US and Israel. FRANCE 24's James Vasina reports.

item.title: France condemns Israel as it deports 37 French nationals over Gaza flotilla
item.description: All 37 French nationals detained aboard a Gaza-bound aid flotilla to Turkey were deported by Israel on Thursday. Paris summoned a senior Israeli diplomat over a video showing the country's national security minister taunting the multinational group of activists while they were being detained.

item.title: Israel: Video of security minister taunting flotilla activists sparks outrage
item.description: Israel's security minister sparked outrage at home and abroad after he showed himself taunting activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla bound and forced to their knees following their arrest by Israeli troops. Foreign ministers from many countries have denounced a "monstrous" treatment, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has denounced actions "not in line with Israel's values".

item.title: Israeli minister Ben-Gvir's video of Gaza flotilla activists sparks outcry
item.description: Detained activists, their hands tied and forced to kneel as the Israeli national anthem is belted out in the background. Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir released footage on X of him taunting the activists from a Gaza-bound flotilla. The video sparked widespread international condemnations. FRANCE 24’s Gabrielle Nadler reports.
